messages:
Ash: heads up — after yesterday's kernel swap we see a ~12–18% p95 tail regression on Mixtral MoE serving for the chat workload. Regression surface: topk=2, batch_size>=8. Any quick theories?

infra-bot: deploy finished: kernel-release-2026-03-16 by @Zane :white_check_mark:

Priya: noticed the router logits distribution shifted. KL divergence between baseline and new kernel increased — more extreme peaks, so a few experts get hammered. Could be numerics in the new fused-softmax.

Zane: running a low-overhead trace now. Early suspicion: fused-softmax uses a different reduction/eps handling in fp16 which slightly changes ordering -> different top-k choices -> load imbalance -> extra cross-expert comms.

Marta: that would explain higher remote KV fetches. If different experts are chosen, KV cache locality drops and we get cache churn.

Priya: perf counters support that: +30% remote-KV reads in affected traces, and +15% memcpy time due to cross-device expert spill.

Ash: can you share a repro command?

Zane: run: ```./perf/repro.sh --model mixtral-7b-moe --batch 16 --topk 2 --route-temp 0.6 --kernels fused-softmax```

Priya: quick test: toggled to legacy-softmax and p95 returned to baseline. Deterministic difference.

Marta: short-term mitigations: lower route-temp to 0.5 or increase topk to 4 to smooth expert load. Long-term: align numerics or add a stable-topk selector.

Ash: can we add a routing-stability CI check that compares topk sets between kernels?

Zane: will do. Plan: harness that runs 100 random prompts, compute jaccard(topk_legacy, topk_new) per-request, and fail if mean < 0.9 or >10% of requests have jaccard < 0.6.

infra-bot: perf-suite queued: job/87421 (ETA ~30m)

Priya: also prototyped a batching heuristic: when estimated expert-imbalance > 0.25, split the batch into two smaller micro-batches. In local sim that dropped p95 by ~11% without throughput loss.

Ash: :thumbsup: good work. Let's rollback the fused-softmax for GA, add the CI stability test, and ship the batching heuristic as an experiment. Add notes to the release ticket.

Zane: adding jenkins job and PR for the harness now.

Priya: I'll open a small RFC to document kernel numerics expectations + acceptance criteria for MoE kernels.

Marta: logging note — include per-request topk hashes and expert-locality score so postmortem is easier if this recurs.

Ash: cool. Assigning follow-ups: Zane (harness + rollback), Priya (RFC + batching patch), Marta (telemetry).
